what_changed_and_it_is_all_on_the_shared: `idle_ready.pelvis.rz +5` — the weight goes on one leg and the hip line rises.
`idle_ready.thigh_l.rz -5`, `thigh_r.rz -5` — both legs counter-roll so they still hang vertical under a rolled pelvis instead of the whole body leaning.
`idle_ready.spine_00.rz -5`, `spine_02.rz -6` — the spine counter-curves so the SHOULDER line tilts OPPOSITE the hip line. Signs opposite is what makes it contrapposto rather than a lean.
`idle_ready.neck.rz +5` — the head stays near level over tilted shoulders, which is what a real neck does.
`idle_ready.thigh_l.rx +8.248`, `calf_l.rx -16.496` — the FREE leg's knee bends. See the foot section: this is solved, not styled.

`idle_loop.pelvis.rz [[0,0],[1.5,1.2],[3,0]]` and `idle_loop.spine_02.rz [[0,0],[1.5,-0.9],[3,0]]` — the weight SHIFTS, which is the half of C3 that asks the two frames to differ. Both curves close at phase 3.0.
2_the_stance_THE_LARGEST_VISIBLE_WIN_IN_.the_spine_number_was_SOLVED_not_tuned: My first attempt used spine_00 -3 / spine_02 -4 and read only -2.313 deg of shoulder tilt, and I did not understand why. Rather than nudge it I measured the sensitivity of every candidate bone: `spine_00.rz +10` moves shoulder tilt **+9.929** (1:1), `clavicle_l.rz +10` moves it +1.084, `clavicle_r.rx +10` moves it +0.097. The answer was not attenuation at all — **the pelvis is the spine's parent, so the +5 pelvis roll carries the whole torso and ADDS +5 to the shoulder line.** -0.313 + 5 - 7 = -2.31, exactly what I read. So the spine must counter-roll by MORE than the pelvis: wanting -6 gives a spine total of -6 - 5 + 0.313 = -10.7, i.e. -5 and -6, which reads -6.297. That is r8's warning about the hem sweep taken seriously: three measured points beat two guesses.

**WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE BAR, AND IT IS A CORPUS FINDING:** `RI-VIS10` C3 asks for 3 degrees of asymmetry. Every reference above is FAR past 3 degrees — the Leyndell soldier is tens of degrees of torso yaw and a visibly dropped shoulder. **3 degrees is the threshold at which a figure stops being provably a mannequin, not the threshold at which it starts looking like these.** My build now passes C3 at 5-6 degrees and still does not look like the plates. The item's own provenance note says every threshold in it is `constructed` and 'not one of them has been validated against a measured population'; C3's 3 degrees is a candidate for the first re-derivation, and the population to derive it from is sitting in `refs/characters/`.
hazards_worth_recording: **`f10-r8-torso.mjs` HAS BEEN MEASURING THE TRUNK IN AN ATTACK POSE.** Its default is `pose: 'idle'` (line 63), and `clips.json` has **no archetype called `idle`** — the names are `idle_loop` and `idle_ready`. Line 277 is `clips.archetypes[opts.pose] || Object.values(clips.archetypes)[0]`, and `Object.keys(j.archetypes)[0]` is **`cut_diagonal`**. So r8's headline trunk numbers were measured mid-swing. They are not wrong — the trunk is the trunk — but the tool's own banner says `idle` and it is not idle, and a lookup that falls back to 'whatever is first in the file' is one key rename away from silently measuring something else again.

**A `git checkout` OF A FILE YOU HAVE ALREADY BANKED IS A NO-OP, AND IT MADE ONE OF MY COMPARISONS VACUOUS.** I ran a before/after of `f10-r8-torso.mjs` by restoring `clips.json` with `git checkout` — after I had banked it. Git printed `Updated 0 paths from the index` and both arms ran on MY file; the two rows were identical and I nearly read that as 'my change does not affect the trunk'. **Identical arms are the signature of a control that did not happen** (RULES rule 6). Redone against a copy taken with `git show HEAD:...` BEFORE the bank, the arms differ: TRUNK waist_pinch 0.1777 -> 0.1728, FIGURE hip_flare 0.9948 -> **1.0647**.

**`tools/land.mjs --paths` IS COMMA-SEPARATED, NOT SPACE-SEPARATED.** `--paths a b` lands `a` and silently treats `b` as commit BODY TEXT. It reported `1 path(s)` and `verified 1 path(s)` and exited 0, which is a truthful message that reads as success — HAZARDS §6's exact shape. I only caught it because I ran `git ls-files` afterwards. **Check the path COUNT against what you meant to land, every time.**

**A PELVIS ROLL LIFTS A FOOT, AND NOTHING IN THE POSE PIPELINE NOTICES.** Rolling the pelvis 5 deg raises the `thigh_r` joint 8.7 mm and lowers `thigh_l` 8.6 mm, so two straight legs put one foot 17.4 mm off the ground on FLAT terrain. No gate fires: `anim-tune` measures weapon sockets, `actor-orbit-holes` measures silhouette holes, and neither looks at whether the feet are level. The only reason I found it is that I checked `foot_l`/`foot_r` world Y by hand. **If you rotate anything at or above the pelvis, measure the feet.**

**THE BASH TOOL BACKGROUNDS A COMMAND AT 120 s AND THAT IS NOT THE SAME AS `run_in_background`.** My Pod run and one `actor-orbit-holes` run were both moved to the background automatically. HAZARDS §13 forbids ENDING A TURN waiting; it does not forbid this. I did the correct thing per §13's replacement #2 — did other work and read the output file later in the same turn — but the trap is real: a command you did not background can still come back as a notification, and treating that notification as permission to stop is the §13 failure with a different cause. `actor-orbit-holes` needs ~86 s and a 300 s explicit tool timeout to run in the foreground.
